text:
violet: FYI ran int3 throughput trials on candidate-b and saw paraphrase anchor collisions spike. paraphrase_recall -19% vs baseline; anchor_collision_rate 0.29 (was 0.06). failing ids at s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase/candidate-b/fails-6845678901.txt :frowning:

anya: That's a big jump. Was tokenization or dedupe changed between manifests? Any manifest-level transforms applied in the ingest?

violet: Ingest pipeline unchanged. I suspect the quant kernel is folding some token encodings. Added metric `identical_first_10_tokens` and it went from 0.07 -> 0.35 on int3 run.

kevin: Could be prefix normalization in the quant path. Before we loop infra, can we trim duplicates via adaptive dedupe and see how much of the drop is dataset? Run command: `curate fuzzy-dedupe --in s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase/candidate-b/manifest.json --out s3://tmp/dedup-0.84.json --threshold 0.84 --keep-anchors 4500`

violet: Ran that. Dedup @0.84 removes ~8.8% anchors. Even after dedupe synthetic sample shows recall still -14%. So dataset dupes explain some but not all.

marta: We can fast-label the dedup-reduced set. Capacity ~520/day if we use compact UI (anchor + single-line context). Want me to create queue?

violet: Yes please. sampler=paraphrase-adaptive-0.84, priority=high. Also mark "anchor-preserve" candidates to avoid accidentally removing canonical anchors.

labelops_bot: Label queue created: queue_id=lab-q-2026-03-26-42, size=736, sampler=paraphrase-adaptive-0.84, priority=high

kevin: Parallel path: I'll repro the eval with an FP16 fallback and also with a canary kernel flag `--preserve-anchor-encoding` to test if preserving raw token encodings helps. Commands I used: 
```
./eval_run --model candidate-b:int3 --prompts s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase/candidate-b/manifest.json \
  --out ./runs/candidate-b-int3-debug.json --kv-debug --fallback fp16
./eval_run --model candidate-b:int3 --prompts s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase/candidate-b/manifest.json \
  --out ./runs/candidate-b-int3-canary.json --kv-debug --kernel-flag preserve-anchor-encoding
```

runtime-ci: We have a canary build with the flag. I'll schedule a 30m window and post results here. If canary aligns with fp16, we can fast-track a kernel patch.

anya: Also let's add a console metric `frac_identical_kv_prefix_first12` and a daily chart so we can see regression trend across profiles. If the kernel flag reduces that metric it's a smoking gun.

violet: FP16 fallback run done: recall within 2% baseline. Canary run with preserve-anchor-encoding also brought recall back to within 3%. Traces: s3://redwood-runs/candidate-b/int3-canary-6845678901.json

kevin: That suggests quant kernel normalization is the culprit. Two options: (A) ship kernel patch with preserve-anchor-encoding, (B) expand golden anchors + relabel to cover edge prefixes. I prefer (A) but prepare (B) as fallback.

marta: Labelers ready. I'll split lab-q-2026-03-26-42 into 4 shards (184 each). I'll include an instruction to "preserve canonical anchor" and tag ambiguous merges `needs-panel` so the golden panel can decide. ETA first shard EOD PST.

labelops_bot: Queue update: shard1=184 assigned, shard2..4 queued. Progress URL: https://labels.redwood/queues/lab-q-2026-03-26-42

runtime-ci: Canary verified match to fp16. Opening runtime issue RUNTIME-1138 and scheduling a patch candidate. We'll hold auto-rollout of int3 profile until patch lands and regression pass completes.

anya: Good. Kevin please add 200 synthetic anchors that perturb early tokens (swap, insert, sub) into `s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase/candidate-b/synthetics/early-token-200.json` and reserve 150 golden-review slots for them. That will give us coverage for future quant kernels.

kevin: Will do. Command I'll use: `python tools/synth_perturb.py --src s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase/candidate-b/golden.json --out s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase/candidate-b/synthetics/early-token-200.json --ops swap,insert,sub --n 200`

violet: Thanks all. Block int3 auto-rollout until RUNTIME-1138 lands and lab queue finishes. I'll post a follow-up in 12hrs or when shard1 completes.
